source.title: Parasympathetic reactivation after maximal CPET depends on exercise modality and resting vagal activity in healthy men.

confidence_rationale: Quantifies parasympathetic reactivation as a process with its own KINETICS (heart-rate recovery + 30-s windowed rMSSD trajectories) whose RATE is set by resting vagal tone -- direct support for modelling recovery as a tunable rate parameter (the smallest-form question). Discounted because the stressor is maximal exercise, not an aversive/psychological stressor, so the transfer to a suffering-recovery process is by analogy on the autonomic-recovery-rate construct only.
failure_signatures: Parasympathetic reactivation rate depended on the exercise modality AND on resting vagal activity -- recovery rate is not a fixed constant but a context- and baseline-conditioned parameter, so a single hard-coded REE recovery_rate would mis-model agents in different states.

Reactivation was slower when resting vagal tone was lower -- a depleted baseline predicts impaired recovery, the same coupling Thayer/Mezzacappa report; a REE rebound that ignored current state would over-recover a depleted agent.

mapping.source_claim_statement: After maximal cardiopulmonary exercise, parasympathetic reactivation (indexed by heart-rate recovery and 30-s-windowed rMSSD) follows a measurable time course whose magnitude/rate depends on exercise modality and on resting cardiac autonomic control; delta-rMSSD into recovery correlated positively with resting HF/rMSSD/SDNN and negatively with resting LF:HF.
mapping.ree_translation: Recovery of autonomic state is a process with its own KINETICS -- a rate, not an instantaneous reset -- and that rate is conditioned by the agent's baseline state. This directly supports the candidate's smallest computational form: an offset-triggered TRANSIENT MULTIPLIER on the MECH-219 recovery_rate / SD-032e drive_bias leak, scaled by current state, rather than a fixed decay constant. The baseline-tone dependence maps onto making the rebound boost a function of current accumulator/drive state.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The stressor is maximal physical exercise, not an aversive/psychological event; parasympathetic reactivation after exercise and recovery from an aversive episode are not the same physiology. The paper is used only for the GENERIC point that autonomic recovery has a tunable, baseline-conditioned rate -- not for any quantitative parameter value. Healthy young men only.
mapping.source_context: 20 healthy men (17-28 yr); three maximal CPET modalities (cycling, walking, running); HRR at 1-3 min post-exercise and rMSSD in consecutive 30-s windows during recovery.

confidence_components.notes: Solid kinetics measurement supporting 'recovery is a tunable, baseline-conditioned rate'. Higher transfer risk: exercise-recovery physiology, not aversive-state recovery; used for the rate-parameter principle only, not values.
